header:
Date: 2026-09-15 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Cascade Tech), Ava Thompson (Head of MLOps), Samir Gupta (Engineer)
summary: Initial PLG quickstart discovery. Cascade Tech evaluating Redwood hosted API for prototyping with potential move to Dedicated for production. Discussed time-to-first-token, free credits, security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), expected throughput and latency tradeoffs. Agreed to POC benchmarks and follow-up security docs.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options
Security: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
Benchmark plan: latency, throughput, cost per token
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, i have Ethan our SE here too. good to meet you all.
[00:07] Jordan: Hey Maya, thanks yeah excited, we just want to understand how fast we can get going — time-to-first-token, free credits, the usual.
[00:15] Ethan: Cool. Quick agenda — quickstart flow, security, then dig into traffic and benchmarks.
[00:23] Ava: Sounds good, real quick context: we run inference for a customer support summarization workflow, about 50k monthly queries today, spiky traffic, peak about 50 qps. Latency SLO is 300ms p95 for short chat completions.
[00:40] Maya: Got it, that's helpful. Is that currently yourselves hosting models or using another API?
[00:45] Jordan: We use ModelX for embeddings and OpenAI for chat right now but cost is creeping up and we want more control — maybe switch to Redwood hosted first then Dedicated later.
[00:55] Ethan: Totally typical. For quickstart, you can sign up, we give test credits — we usually provision $1k free credits for evaluation teams, which should cover initial benchmark runs and a small POC. Time-to-first-token is usually minutes from signup to calling the REST API; we have quickstart SDKs and sample prompts.
[01:12] Samir: When you say minutes, do you mean getting a key and calling an endpoint for a real model? Or are there manual steps?
[01:20] Maya: It's fully self-serve. Create account, verify email, get API key, call the /generate endpoint. We've seen devs get first token in under 10 minutes if they follow the quickstart. If you want us to pre-provision credits and a test key we can do that.
[01:33] Jordan: Nice. What about Dedicated — how long to move to reserved capacity?
[01:38] Ethan: Dedicated typically takes a few weeks to provision depending on region and capacity. There's a provisioning lead time for GPU pools, and we'll coordinate a cutover plan. For many customers we do hybrid: start hosted for dev and POC, then reserve Dedicated for production traffic.
[01:50] Ava: Important for us: VPC peering and KMS integration, we need keys in our HSM and audit logs for compliance.
[01:57] Maya: Yes, we support Private deployments and VPC options. Our Private control plane supports customer-managed networking; KMS/HSM integration is supported — we map to your key handles. We also provide audit logs and role-based access control.
[02:08] Jordan: Is Redwood SOC 2?
[02:11] Maya: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II — we'll share the report and the compliance pack.
[02:17] Samir: How about SSO?
[02:19] Ethan: We support SAML and OIDC for enterprise accounts — we can share the SSO integration guide.
[02:25] Jordan: Ok good. On performance: our main ask is p95 latency under 300ms for 1k token responses — is that realistic on hosted?
[02:34] Ethan: Depends on model choice and batching. For shorter completions and a small model like the 7B open model, you can be sub-300ms on good infra for single token latency, but for 1k tokens that's larger. Some customers use quantized models and kernel optimizations. For strict SLOs many choose Dedicated to pin capacity and reduce variance.
[02:55] Ava: Can you explain caching — prefix/KV cache — we have repeated prefixes across many calls.
[03:01] Ethan: Sure. Redwood has prefix/KV caching — if you have common context we can cache KV pairs and serve tokens faster and cheaper. That reduces per-token compute and cost. We also do continuous batching to improve throughput.
[03:15] Jordan: Are there limits on model selection in hosted?
[03:18] Maya: We have a model catalog with curated open models and variants. Hosted supports a large set; for Dedicated/Private you can bring certain model families; there are compatibility checks.
[03:27] Samir: Any gotchas with rate limiting or quotas during POC?
[03:31] Maya: We'll set relaxed quotas for the POC, but production needs defined rate limits. We can set per-route quotas and bursts.
[03:38] Ava: We need to run benchmarks — what's the best way to do that?
[03:42] Ethan: We'll share a benchmark plan: sample prompts, load generator scripts, and target metrics: p50/p95 latency, throughput (qps), token cost. For POC we recommend baseline on hosted then repeat on Dedicated to compare unit economics.
[03:56] Jordan: Ok, and pricing — is it strictly per-token on hosted?
[03:59] Maya: Hosted is usage based (per-token), Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) — we can give a cost model showing break-even points. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching to lower per-token cost.
[04:12] Samir: How often do you see quality regressions when switching quantization?
[04:15] Ethan: We run evals tied to prompt sets; small quality diffs can appear at lower bit quantization — we recommend running your evaluation harness. We also have rollback and model variant routing to mitigate regressions.
[04:29] Jordan: For the quickstart, can we get test data loaded somehow or do we need to run locally?
[04:35] Maya: You can upload prompt sets to the console or run locally — for the POC we usually ask customers to run the load generator from their env to simulate network and auth. We'll provide scripts and a sample deck.
[04:47] Ava: Any security concerns with sending prompts to hosted?
[04:50] Ethan: We have data retention controls and optional no-retention modes for enterprise. For regulated data, many customers choose Private or Dedicated with VPC and on-prem options.
[04:59] Jordan: Competitors question — are there features you think make Redwood stand out versus Anthropic/OpenAI?
[05:05] Maya: We focus on production economics: the runtime, batching, KV cache, and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. Plus observability and rollout controls.
[05:14] Samir: Awesome. A couple of clarifying technical questions — do you support quantized LLMs and how do you handle KV cache warmup?
[05:21] Ethan: Yes quantization is supported; kernel selection and execution paths are quantization-friendly. KV cache warmup depends on traffic patterns; we can pre-warm cache for predictable prefixes or rely on automatic prefix caching for repeated patterns.
[05:34] Jordan: Timeline: we want to spin up a POC in the next two weeks. Is that realistic?
[05:38] Maya: Yes, totally. We'll provision credits and a test key today or tomorrow, you run benchmarks, and we reconvene after results. If you want Dedicated we can start the sizing conversations in parallel.
[05:49] Ava: For the Dedicated sizing, what inputs do you need?
[05:52] Ethan: Peak qps, tokens per request, p95 latency target, model family, and retention/throughput. Also region preference and whether you need burst capacity.
[06:03] Jordan: I'll send traffic profile.
[06:05] Samir: Are there example decks or runbooks for on-prem/private installs?
[06:08] Maya: Yes we have a private deployment runbook; will share the link in the follow-up.
[06:13] Jordan: Ok great.
[06:15] Maya: Quick recap — action items: Maya to send pricing and SOC2 pack, Ethan to prep benchmark plan, Jordan to share traffic profile. We'll also provision quickstart credits and test key. Anything else?
[06:28] Ava: Could you also share the SSO guide and KMS integration notes?
[06:31] Maya: Yep.
[06:33] Jordan: Thanks folks, this was helpful.
[06:35] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and schedule the POC kickoff.
[06:40] [call ends]
